1.
Heard learned counsel for the appellant, learned A.G.A. for the State and learned counsel for the complainant.

2. The instant criminal appeal has been preferred by the appellant under Section 14A(2) of SC/ST Act against the order dated 10.09.2024 passed by learned Special Judge (SC/ST Act), Varanasi in Bail Application No. 3333 of 2024 (Sandeep Kumar Patel Vs.State of U.P.) in Case Crime No. 286 of 2024 under Sections 376, 377, 328, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3 (1) (Dha), 3(2) (V) of SC/ST Act, P.S.- Shivpur, District -Varanasi.

sentences.text: As per the prosecution case in brief, victim got a First Information Report lodged on 11.07.2024 against the appellant making allegations inter alia that appellant who is resident of her neighbouring village is debauched boy and used to visit her village and by taking her under his influence, started visiting her house.
He lured her and started making physical relation with her giving false promise of marriage.

When she asked for marriage, appellant putting vermilion in her forehead said now you are my wife and also said the he after convincing his parents as well as uncle and aunt, will take her to his house.

Later, on her insistence, appellant refused to marry her saying that she belongs to scheduled caste, that's why she cannot get married at our house but after 15 days,
appellant again came to her house after tendering apology, took her to visit Devi Temple and gave her tea on the way, after sometime she found herself in a closed room with him without clothes.
When she asked about her condition, appellant told her that he has made physical relation with her and also made her obscene video and took photos.

Thereafter, the appellant by blackmailing her kept changing place day by day and made physical relation with her.
3.

It is submitted by learned counsel for the appellant that there are several contradictions with regard to the prosecution case in F.I.R. as well as in the statements under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C. of the victim, therefore, victim's statement is not liable to be believed.
It is next submitted that there is delay in lodging F.I.R. and that too without any plausible explanation.

It is also pointed out that the victim, in her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C., has disclosed her age about 22 years,
whereas, she in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., disclosed her age about 32 years.

Lastly it is submitted that considering the statements of the victim, it can be concluded that she was a consenting party with the appellant and she went to meet appellant in jail disclosing her identity as appellant's sister, as such it is not a case of making forceful physical relation with her by the appellant.
The appellant has no criminal history to his credit and is languishing in jail since 13.07.2024, therefore he may be released on bail.

4. On the other hand, learned A.G.A. as well as learned counsel for the complainant have vehemently opposed the submissions of learned counsel for the appellant by contending that appellant on the false promise to marry, demanded sexual favour from victim.
Initially she refused but because of her promise of marriage, victim consented for sexual intercourse.
This act was repeated multiple times.
Every time she consented for the physical relations only for the reason that accused had promised to marry her.
Much emphasis has been given by contending that intention of accused-appellant was malafide and he had clandestine motive since beginning.
Such a fraudulent act cannot said to be consensual.
Since victim in the F.I.R. as well as in her statements has made specific allegation of rape against the appellant, hence, the bail application of the appellant is liable to be rejected.

5. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and examined the matter in its entirety, this Court is of the view that consent of a women u/s 375 I.P.C. is vitiated on the ground of a misconception of the facts where such misconception was the basis for her choosing to engage her sexual relation.

In the context of a promise to marry it is well settled that there is a distinction between a false promise given on the understanding by the maker that it will be broken, and the breach of promise which is made in good faith but subsequently not fulfilled.

Sandeep Kumar Patel vs State Of U.P. And Another on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179679081/
2 6.

entities.text: Sandeep Kumar Patel vs State Of U.P. And Another on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Anurag Soni vs. State of Chhattisgarh, (2019) 13 SCC 1, has held that where the promise to marry is false and the intention of maker at the time of making the promise itself was not to abide by it but to deceive the women to convince her to engage in sexual relations, there is a "misconception of facts" that vitiates the women "consent " u/s 375 I.P.C.
7.

entities.text: Anurag Soni vs. State of Chhattisgarh, (2019) 13 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Niranjan Singh and Another vs. Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote and Others, AIR 1980 SC 785, has avoided detailed examination of the evidence and elaborate documentation of the merits of the case as no party should have the impression that his case has been prejudiced.

entities.text: Niranjan Singh and Another vs. Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote and Others, AIR 1980 SC 785
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A prima facie satisfaction of the case is needed but it is not the same as an exhaustive exploration of the merits in the order itself.

8. Considering the allegation of the victim as mentioned in the FIR as well as in her statements recorded during the course of investigation, I do not find any good ground to disbelieve the statements of the victim at this stage and to presume the false implication of the appellant.

9. So far as order dated 06.09.2024 passed by the co-ordinate bench of this Court in Criminal Misc.
Bail Application No. 3361 of 2024 (Nilesh Chauhan @ Guddu vs. State of U.P.) relied upon by the counsel for the appellant, is concerned it is relevant to mention that every case turns on its own facts.

entities.text:
Criminal Misc.
Bail Application No. 3361 of 2024 (Nilesh Chauhan @ Guddu vs. State of U.P.)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even one additional or different fact may make a big difference between the conclusion in two cases, because even a single significant detail may alter the entire aspect.
The said case is distinguishable on the facts of this case.
10. In view of the above, the present criminal appeal lacks merit and is accordingly, dismissed.
